notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I haven't written any notes. Every time I tried to open a source page, the tool returned "You have no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn." That tool is my only way to search or open the approved sites; the other tools I have can't reach the internet. As a result, I didn't read a single page from Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes or any of the other sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and fill no gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written verse notes from memory. They would have no real sources behind them, and any URLs I gave would be guesses rather than pages I had checked.

**What I'll do when the tool works again** (in a new message, or once the limit resets):

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - Enduring Word on Proverbs 3
   - Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight
   - Precept Austin's Proverbs 3 page
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** the likely places are:
   - vv. 5–6 (trust and guidance)
   - vv. 9–10 (firstfruits, tithing and blessing)
   - vv. 11–12 (discipline, tied to Hebrews 12)
   - v. 34 (grace to the humble, quoted in James 4 and 1 Peter 5)

   I'd look for each tradition's own teachers on these, for example Wesley's notes, Spurgeon, Desiring God, Ligonier and the LCMS.
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible translators' notes, for example on the wording in vv. 3, 6, 8 and 32
   - Bible Odyssey on Lady Wisdom (vv. 13–20)
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings, for example the Church Fathers reading v. 19's wisdom as Christ
   - Prosperity readings of vv. 9–10 and 16, as Got Questions and similar sites describe and critique them

If you send the request again, I'll start with these sources and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for each point.
